source_evidence.finding: _execute runs the executor, then reconnects and writes terminal state to SQLite. close sets shutdown, cancels queued/running rows and child processes, joins workers only until a shared 1.5-second deadline, then returns while retaining any live workers. A blocked executor can therefore outlive close and later access the database.

test_close_releases_workers_and_rejects_new_jobs uses _manager's immediate-success lambda; it checks no workers remain but does not hold an executor beyond the 1.5-second join deadline. No close-timeout stress case observed in the bounded test-name/worker-assert search.
benchmark cleanup calls app.close() and then owned_scratch.cleanup(); if close returns with a worker alive, its SQLite file can be removed before the worker's final database access.
